NEW YORK MINUTE / AN EXPERIMENT IN TIME & PLACE
EVERY PHOTOGRAPH WAS A PRESENT MOMENT.

The city keeps time.

At each minute, this clock looks for a New York photograph whose camera recorded that same time of day. The photograph might be from yesterday or from years ago.

When a minute has no match, the previous photograph stays. The clock carries on. The caption always shows the photograph’s own recorded time.

A different day, a different view.

When several photographs match, we use a stable daily selection across photographers and photographic sequences. A refresh keeps the same choice; a new day can bring another view. Image availability can change that choice.

About the collection

This first edition uses a research collection from Wikimedia Commons.

Most camera timestamps do not have a verified time zone in this collection; we provisionally treat them as local to New York. Camera clocks can be wrong. Photos are selected using metadata, and the collection has not been fully visually reviewed.

This edition uses a saved collection from October 23, 2026. Automatic discovery and synchronization with Wikimedia are not connected yet.

Photographs belong to their respective creators. Each image links to its source and license and is displayed without cropping or alteration. The clock always follows America/New_York, including daylight saving time.
